Niche subjects: every school, every available year

England, key stage 4 · 2021/22 · 2022/23 · 2023/24 · 2024/25 · generated 2026-09-07 01:49 from DfE data, read-only

Table 3 of the To-Build page lists the small subjects and the ten largest centres in each. This page is the whole list, and it adds time. For every subject with 3,000 or fewer England entries in 2024/25 — plus the languages named alongside them that sit just over the line — it takes every school that entered a pupil in any year the data covers, lines the years up side by side, and says what kind of centre it is.

The classes are simple. NEW means the school's first entries fall in 2023/24 or 2024/25 — a course that has just started, whose teacher is still building the resources and has nothing on the shelf. That is the warmest prospect on the page. ESTABLISHED means entries in every year from 2022/23 onwards: a real department, harder to displace but worth more when it lands. ALTERNATE means the entries skip a year at a time, which is the ordinary shape of a small cohort taught every other year, not a school losing interest — the approach is to check where they are in the cycle. INTERMITTENT is the same idea with a longer gap. LAPSED means entries earlier but none in 2024/25, and ONE-OFF means a single year that is not the latest. Both are cold.

What the numbers cannot tell you

  • England only. The source counts pupils at the end of key stage 4 in English schools and colleges. Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland are absent, so a WJEC-heavy subject looks smaller here than it is.
  • Independent schools are in. The performance tables cover independent centres that enter pupils, and for Classical Greek, Latin, Ancient History and Hebrew they dominate. The Type column says which is which, and an independent school buys very differently from a state one.
  • Two exam years are missing and cannot be recovered. Summer 2020 and summer 2021 were centre-assessed and teacher-assessed; no exams were sat and DfE published no performance tables. 2018/19 exists but the download service no longer serves it. So the deepest series available anywhere is four years, and a school that taught a subject through the pandemic and stopped in 2022 is invisible.
  • A single latest-year appearance is ambiguous. One entry in 2024/25 and nothing before reads as NEW, but it is equally consistent with a departing teacher's last cohort, a private candidate sitting at a nearby centre, or a single pupil entered for a heritage language they already speak. For the heritage languages that last case is the common one, which is why Polish, Chinese and Portuguese show thousands of schools and almost no departments.
  • Alternate-year cohorts are real. A school with eight takers often runs the option every other year. Do not read a one-year gap as a loss.
  • The vocational groups were re-coded in 2023/24. DfE folded BTEC First, WJEC Level 1/2, AQA Technical Award and most VRQ rows into a single "Level 1/Level 2 vocational qualification" bucket, and re-cut several subject discount groups at the same time. Rows where that shows are marked TAXONOMY BREAK and only their last two years are compared. Every vocational row also rolls all Level 1/2 awarding routes together, because a school switching from a BTEC to a Cambridge National is still teaching the subject.
  • Entries are not pupils on roll. They are exam entries counted at the end of KS4, so a school entering the same pupil for two routes appears twice in the family total.

Where the data comes from

Two DfE sources, both read-only, recorded in full in scripts/_planning/dfe_datasets.json.

Explore Education Statistics. The publication “Key stage 4 performance” (c8756008-ed50-4632-9b96-01b5ca002a43) carries a school-level subject data set for 2024/25 only, as API data set 1ae39901-b462-df76-b108-640a078d7944 — the one this repo already queries for dfe_subject_entries_2025.json. The 2023/24 release carries the same table as a plain CSV data-set file with no API data set. The 2022/23, 2021/22, 2020/21 and 2019/20 releases carry no school-level subject file at all, so the EES API on its own cannot give a multi-year series.

School performance tables download service. Publishes the same underlying table — KS4 underlying data, entries and grades — for 2021/22 to 2024/25 under one schema, as england_ks4underlying_entriesandgrades_2.xlsx. That is the series used here. As a check, every one of the 34 subject totals this page computes for 2024/25 from the performance tables matches the figure the EES API returns, to the entry.

Sources: DfE Explore Education Statistics API (key stage 4 performance) and the DfE school performance tables download service (download data). Row filter: grade “Total number entered”. Built by scripts/_planning/fetch_dfe_history.py and scripts/_planning/render_niche_history.py.
